findings.claim: Reusing one Electron process across multiple geometries contaminated later cases and could not prove the production fix.
findings.evidence: The harness produced a correct first navigation and scrollTop zero on subsequent cases. One geometry per Electron process removed lifecycle state from the oracle.
findings.path: workflow matrix -> Electron process -> BrowserWindow fixture lifecycle

findings.claim: A virtualized DOM shrink can reclamp an accepted programmatic scroll position to the new bottom and emit a later scroll event that the single numeric token misclassifies as user input.
findings.evidence: Instrumented Electron 43.4.0 at DPR 1.25 showed accepted scrollTop 154.4 at scrollHeight 568, then a later event at scrollTop 0 and scrollHeight 414 changed following to false. The new current-bottom rule and regression close this path.
findings.path: Renderer DOM mutation -> Chromium reclamp -> scroll event -> WTerm ownership classifier
